reasons: Classification is sound: the only ownership provision (p0029) runs one way in TrueLink's favour, and nothing in the cited text gives Client ownership of, or a perpetual licence to, the Support Services work product, nor confirms retention of rights in Client Content/Client IP/borrower and loan data — so the clause set fails even the fallback (perpetual, royalty-free licence to deliverables), not merely the preferred position.

Redline is additive and minimal: the existing TrueLink Interface ownership sentence is left intact and a new subsection (e) is inserted covering the three elements the rule requires (Customer Data/Client IP retention, assignment of Work Product with licence-back for embedded Vendor IP, and no joint ownership). It creates no assignment of Client IP or data to the Vendor, consistent with the deterministic checks.

Comment is accurate, correctly scoped and in the required tone: it states what was added and why, cites the 'we own what we pay for and what we put in' position, and expressly preserves TrueLink's ownership of the Interface.

Reasonable judgment not to double-flag section 8(d): a term-limited, Non-Competition-Agreement-bound licence over narrowly defined Credit Data is a licence, not an assignment, so it is noted in the rationale rather than redlined — consistent with the playbook's no-duplicate-flagging and vendor-benefit rules.

Minor, non-fatal drafting points only: the inserted text uses capitalised terms ('Client Intellectual Property', 'TrueLink Intellectual Property') that may not be formally defined in the agreement, and 'Work Product' as drafted could arguably reach Interface enhancements — both are curable in negotiation and do not undermine the finding.
